properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/23/2024 to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Middlebury Township, Tioga county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/22/2024
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8188372
Permit API: 117-22214
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/23/2024
Comments: On 5/23/2024 at 0830 hrs., Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) representative John Rogers conducted an Incident - Response to Accident or Event Inspection (INCDT) of the Seneca Resources - Bauer 849 well pad located in Middlebury Twp, Tioga Co. Complaint Id: 380888.I met Seneca's Jeff Passerrello and Mark McCormick when I arrived at the site. Jeff explained the event as follows: A Nextier frac fleet is on site performing stimulation operations on seven recently drilled wells. The crew is currently zippering between two wells, the 68HU and the 69HU. A BTI water hauling truck was offloading produced water into the frac tanks on the south side of the pad. When pressuring up, a pipe fitting on back site tube popped and sprayed out a mist of produced water. The estimated amount of water impacted a 20' x 50' area on the unprotect pad surface. Pictures 4 and 5 were supplied by Seneca personnel, showing the damaged pipe fitting. Pictures 7 and 8 were also supplied by Seneca personnel, showing the stained gravel surface. We viewed the area of the release. The surface of the area has been scraped and new gravel has been installed. The scraped material was temporarily placed on secondary containment, awaiting the arrival of a rolloff dumpster. The crew was installing a secondary containment structure that will contain the rolloff dumpster when it arrives at the site. I field tested water puddles in various areas north of the frac tanks. An 8' x 6' water puddle between the utility trailers field tested at 2.48 mS conductance. 40' x 30' water puddle at the west end of the frac tank secondary containment field tested at 2.19 mS conductance. A 35' x 40' water puddle on the unprotected pad surface about midway along the frac tanks field tested at 2.05 mS conductance. Puddles underneath the secondary containment structure that was being installed for the excavated material roll off dumpster field tested at 1.8 mS conductance. Water in the frac tank secondary containment field test at 19.99 mS conductance. The upper limit of tha Altairs PCTS5 is 19.99 mS conductance. Water in the east end of the offloading catch basin field tested and 18.03 mS conductance. Water in the west end field tested at 4.32 mS conductance. The crew was setting up to vacuum the water from the frac tank secondary containment ant the unloading catch basin. Mark said that he would have the crew suck up the fluid between the utility trailers.The site is stabilized with at least 70% uniform perennial vegetation. PCSM is addressed on site by a detention basin located on the south edge of location. It was adequately stabilized and functioning as designed. I did witness some temporary compost filter socks positioned around the location.The release of well-bore fluids to the unprotected pad surface constitutes violations of these three regulations; SWMA 301, CSL 402(b) and 25 PA Code 78a.56. The spill had been cleaned up, resulting in VIOICs (Violation noted and Immediately Corrected).The DEP recommends the following: 1. Screen the area impacted by the release of well-bore fluids for additional contamination and continue with cleanup as necessary.2. Continue to remove the elevated conductance fluid from the frac tank secondary containment and the unloading catch basin. Train personnel on proper procedures to prevent releasing the elevated conductance fluids into the containments. I left the site at 1045 hours.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington

Inspection Date: 5/14/2025
Comments: On 05/14/2025, an incident inspection was conducted at the Cogar Well Site following an incident report received by the Department on 05/12/2025 (CTS 389093). SPSI crew on site remediating. The operator reported a spill to the Department on 05/13/2025 regarding more than 5 gallons of production water that were released on a load out pumpkin. No waterways were affected. The incident occurred on 05/12/2025 and reported over two hours after the incident on 05/13/2025. The following was observed:The area of impact was adjacent to the containment of the production tanks. SPSI excavated the impacted area to determine the extent of impact and place waste in roll off dumpsters. The area of impact was under the load out pumpkin and where the cement containment would be. A portion of the dump line was exposed during excavation. Water was pooling within the excavated area (Photos 1-6).Conductivity readings were taken within the area of impact. Readings were 5.23, 7.60, 13.62, 14.27, 16.22 mS/cm, and Over Range (Photos 7-14).Additional readings taken within the upper layers of substrate and clay layer were 430, 533, 850, and 968 uS/cm (Photos 15-18).The cement containment had a reading of Over Range. There appeared to be residual fluid combined with rainwater (Photo 19).The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan were on site (Photo 20).Due to the release of production fluid greater than 5 gallons and failure to report a reportable spill within 2 hours, violations of 78a54, SWMA 301, 78a57(a), 91.34(a), 78a66(b)2 are being issued. The Department requests an updated estimation of the quantity of production fluid released. The Department requests information on if the operator intends to remediate per Act 2 guidelines regarding the quantity released.

Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 8154151
Permit API: 051-24067
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Jefferson Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/27/2023
Comments: On July 27 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 3491397,3387914, 3514511 and 3543627. Accompanying into today's inspection was the landowner. The findings were as follows: According to the Order issued to the operator by the Department for this site, the Operator shall completely restore the well site within 9 months after plugging. The well site and access road are not restored during today's inspection, not exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. According to the landowner, the site has not been restored to pre-existing contours.The well was plugged on October 7, 2021 according the the plugging certificate submitted by the Operator for this well. As such, the Operator was to completely restore the well site no later than July 7, 2022. E and S Plan has not been received by the Department as previously requested in IRs 3262679, 3387914, 3514511 and 3543627. No E and S Plan was found on site. Lack of adequate uniform vegetation is still observed due to multiple areas of exposed soil and rock. There are several bare spots throughout the former well site that are lacking adequate uniform vegetation. No E and S BMPs are installed on site. The ground appears to be seeded in most areas, but 70% uniform vegetation has not been achieved at this time. Vegetative growth may be hindered by the amount of rock and gravel on site. The Department recommends the Operator take necessary measures to ensure 70% uniform vegetative growth is achieved for restoration of the site. Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding.The transmission of this inspection is delayed due to an IT error.

Comments: Southwestern's (SWN's) reported to the DEP reporting hotline at ~ 1705 hours on 03/22/2024 that a vendor ripped containment liner while moving hoses during demobilization activities. Ponded rain water ran from containment onto newly exposed soil/gravel. It is believed rainwater came into contact with brine contaminated site equipment releasing approx. 20 to 30 gallons.On 03/26/2024 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of SWN's VanOrder-Patrick (12 Pad) Well Pad located in Herrick Township, Bradford County. The weather was 47 degrees and partly cloudy. I arrived at 1010 hours. This inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to DEP by SWN.On 03/26/2024 I spoke with Mike Deming a SWN representative who said the release was ~1-2 barrels. Photos #2-6 show the progression of the remediation process from 03/22/2024 to 03/26/2024. SWN reported that the highest conductivity reading after the release was ~21 mS/cm. The red dumpster seen in photo #6 is lined and holds the recovered material. Due to active operations during the time of this inspection access to the spill area was not possible. SWN representatives were present during the time of the inspection. SWN representatives said they are currently working on drill outs. They have completed the plugs for one of the three new wells. They plan to finish within two weeks. Pooled water on the pad was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 428-839 us/cm. Pooled water within the off loading secondary containment was field measured for EC at ~ 2.7 mS/cm. The DEP reported the findings to SWN representatives who said that it would be taken care of right away. Based on the reported release quantity this is being referred to Act 2 for compliance. Based on the reported release violations of the following are cited against API #015-23842 at this time:35 P.S. 691.402(b)35 P.S. 6018.30125 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)I departed at 1050 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/09/2024 to GREYLOCK PROD LLC in Hector Township, Potter county. 78a64a(f) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – Operator failed to remove regulated substances that escaped from primary containment or otherwise spilled onto secondary containment as soon as possible and inspect the secondary containment after removal.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: GREYLOCK PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/09/2024
Violation Code: 78a64a(f) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – Operator failed to remove regulated substances that escaped from primary containment or otherwise spilled onto secondary containment as soon as possible and inspect the secondary containment after removal.
Violation ID: 8210427
Permit API: 105-21962
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Hector Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/09/2024
Comments: On 12/09/2024 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1200 hours, weather was 40F and raining. An Act 9 sign and well permits are visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).Stimulation activities for the two recently drilled wells are ongoing, equipment is located onsite to support these activities (photos #2-5). See inspection report #3878285 for more details. The accessible area excavated due to the release noted in inspection report #3878285 has been backfilled and fluids in this area field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at a range of ~701-741us/cm (photo #6). The remaining impacted area from this release will be excavated and backfilled upon removal of the rig matting covering that area. DEP Environmental Cleanups and Brownsfield personnel were onsite prior to my arrival to follow up on the release detailed in inspection report #3878285 and noted concerns regarding a diesel sheen observed on portions of the pad surface.The source of the diesel was investigated by Greylock and it was determined that a maintenance truck located onsite had released an undetermined amount of diesel, the truck was removed from the site and staff were working on removing diesel from the pad surface at the time of this inspection (photos #7-10). Fluid was observed overtopping from the secondary containment structure of the produced fluids offload area onsite (photos #11 and 12). This fluid was combining with rainwater and the diesel sheen on the pad surface and moving into the pad's drainage system which transports water from the pad surface to the site's post-construction stormwater management (PCSM) control. Fluids on the pad surface near the offload containment structure field measured for EC at ~10.32-15.93mS/cm; personnel from Penn E and R measured a similar result of 11.10mS/cm (photos #14-16).The pad drainage system services the site's infiltration basin via two pipes which move fluids from their respective half of the pad (photo #17). One pipe is located closer to the produced fluids offload area and the other is located near the wellheads. Fluid with a diesel sheen was observed discharging into the infiltration basin from the pipe near the offload area; this fluid field measured for EC at ~1.35mS/cm and the soil near this area field measured for EC at ~1.20mS/cm (photos #18-20). Fluid discharging from the pipe near the wellheads field measured for EC at ~0.908mS/cm (photo #21). Vacuum trucks were dispatched to remove fluids from the secondary containment structures and the pad surface in response to the release (photo #22). Personnel were also working to install sump pumps and shut in the drainage pipes to prevent any further discharge into the basin.I followed up with Greylock and they informed me that the drains discharging into the basin were shut in at 1400 hours and they were recovering fluids from basin with a vacuum truck.The DEP recommends the following:-Continuing to prevent fluids from reaching PCSM controls until all contaminated fluids and soils are recovered.-Removing fluids from containment structures as it accumulates.-Following Act 2 to remediate the infiltration basin, diesel spill, and produced fluids containment release.Based on the results of this inspection, the following violations are cited against API #105-21962:-25 PA 78a64a(f) due to the observation of produced fluids overtopping from a secondary containment structure and being conveyed into the sites PCSM controls. -35 P.S. 691.401 due to the release of produced fluids and diesel discharging into the site's PCSM controls.The violations cited in inspection report #3878285 remain outstanding due to the remediation requirements outlined in 25 PA 78a.66(c)(2)(i) having not yet been met.I departed the site at 1345.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/29/2026
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8282743
Permit API: 081-22059
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Jackson Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/29/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that a release of an estimated 20 gallons of produced fluid was released to the pad surface on 7/28/26 at 0244. The notification stated that the fluid was sucked up the same day and impacted soil was excavated and containerized. Work crews were rigging down the drilling rig and associated drilling equipment during this inspection. It rained steadily during this inspection and there was a large volume of stormwater on the pad surface. I met with company man John Hulsey upon arriving on the well pad. He told me that the release occurred in the area of the drilling mud tanks when a jet vac leaked and caused produced fluid to be released to the surface of the pad. I inspected the pad surface and secondary containment for the drilling mud tanks. The fluid on the containment had an electrical conductivity (EC) of 288 uS/cm. The fluid on the pad surface immediately adjacent to the containment berms had an EC of 272 uS/cm. Puddles farther away from the containment on the pad surface had similar readings with none greater than 400 uS/cm. Puddles of stormwater on other areas of the well pad had EC readings of less than 300 uS/cm for each puddle measured. No evidence of produced fluid was observed on the pad surface. The well site secondary containment appeared to be in good condition. No holes were observed in the containment liner.Violations noted against well permit 081-22059 and are considered immediately corrected.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2/13/2025 to PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC in Howe Township, Forest county. SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/13/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 8217501
Permit API: 053-31092
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/13/2025
Comments: This conventional well is equipped for production with a pump jack. A sign labeling the API number, well name, and operator information was posted on the well.This inspection was conducted in response to a phone call from Stuart Morris, a representative from Pennhills Resources, reporting a leak which had occurred at Well 24 (API # 053-31092). Upon arrival to the site, staff from Pennhills were actively working to remediate the issue. The well had been shut in, and a hole approximately 3 feet deep and 6 feet wide was dug near the well head to determine the source of the leak. A broken line was discovered as the source of the leak and was removed and replaced during this inspection. Crude oil was evident in the hole and could be seen within the shale (fill material) of the side walls of the hole. It appears that it's traveling through the fill that was used to build the location. Crude oil appears to have traveled through the stone/fill, and then comes out on the surface in two different areas on the southwest and northwest sides of the well site. The crude oil coming to the surface on the southwest side of the well site primarily collected in a natural depression below the well site with some migrating somewhat linearly in the southwest and west direction for approximately 25 yards. There are several small depressions on the ground surface within the linear track of the migrated crude oil which appear to hold seasonal precipitation and snowmelt. The leaked crude oil can be visually observed in these depressions. The crude oil coming to the surface on the northwest side of the well site appears to have primarily collected in a natural depression below the well site with minimal travel beyond 5 yards from the natural collection point. The amount of crude oil released as a result of this incident is undetermined due to the snow cover and lack of visual surface evidence at the site. A small tributary, denoted as Bald Hill Run (HQ-CWF), flows approximately 50 yards west of the well site. Leaked crude oil on the west side of the well site was last spotted approximately 50 feet away from Bald Hill Run. Bald Hill Run did not appear to be impacted from this incident. Also, a noted wetland is approximately 50 yards from the southwest side of the well site. The leaked crude oil on the southwest side of the well site was last observed approximately 50 feet from the wetland. The wetland did not appear to be impacted from this incident.Booms and diapers were already installed upon arrival within all the depressions where crude oil was visually observed. Booms and diapers should be regularly monitored and replaced as necessary until the site is deemed remediated. It was discussed on site to create collection points and install siphons where necessary as a remediation strategy moving forward. Also, to pump out the crude oil and fluids within the hole before burying. A follow up inspection will occur to document these efforts. Follow up inspections will routinely be conducted to monitor the remediation of the release. Confirmatory field screening and/or sampling will be conducted to verify that cleanup is deemed complete.

The estimated volume of the spill was about 500 gallons of production fluid. The area of impact was about 120 ft. X 150 ft. circle with varying levels of conductivity. Penn E&R is scheduled to collect confirmatory samples on April 20, 2021. This spill causes violations of the Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and the Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. Comments: On 02/08/2021, DEP representative John Ciccone prepared an administrative report regarding Chesapeake Appalachia LLC's (CALLC) Stone BRA pad in Tuscarora Twp., Bradford County. The purpose of this report is to document CALLC's Notice of Violation (NOV) response for NOV 391862 and to upload the response to eFACTS. Details regarding the initial NOV issuance can be found within inspection report # 3141162. On 02/05/2021, CALLC issued their NOV response regarding NOV 391862 via electronic mail. CALLC stated their acknowledgment of violations of 35 P.S. 691.402(b) (Clean Streams Law), 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a) (improper waste storage), and 35 P.S. 6018.301 (Solid Waste Management Act, improper waste storage) due to a produced water release on their Stone BRA pad. The released volume was estimated to be greater than one barrel (42 gallons). The release occurred on the Stone BRA pad, due to a breach in a produced water frac tank containment. CALLC's response identified produced fluids as being the regulated substance involved in the release, in the presence of precipitation. An area of approximately 37 feet by 42 feet by < 1 foot (depth) was delineated via soil conductivity field screening and scraped. 10 post-excavation samples were collected in accordance with systematic random sampling by Creston Environmental, LLC (Creston). Excavated soils were placed within containment, covered, and labeled, awaiting waste characterization for proper disposal. The cause of the containment breach was believed to be caused by a dropped connection hose. CALLC stated that the containment was repaired on 01/30/2021 by Creston. CALLC stated that the release remained isolated on the pad, did not reach or threaten any water supplies or surface waters, and did not impact any buildings or utilities. CALLC plans to document remedial action, associated attainment results, and restoration within an Act 2 deliverable. The information within CALLC's NOV response satisfies the 25 Pa. Code 78a.66c(2)(i). The NOV response has been uploaded to eFACTS with this report.

Inspection Date: 4/07/2022
Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72-hr (Stepped) pressure build-up tests, (SPBUT) being performed on all (6) wells on the Aukema pad. The Aukema 3H, 4H, 7H, 1HC, 2HC and the 101HC wells. These tests are being performed to assess the results of the initial remedial deployment of Renegades localized casing expansion tool in the production casing of the Aukema 1HC and 101HC wells on 5/17/21 and 5/18/21 and the 3H and 2HC between 1/24 - 27/21. This is the third round of testing since initial remedial work was performed. SPBUTs were initiated on 4/4/22 @ ~ 10:00 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - All (6) wells annuli are shut in. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Reps. Craig Shores and Zach Burnett and Creston Consultant Reps., Will Dolan and Jason Rajan. Starting at approx. 10:00, ending annuli pressures were checked using a Digital Crystal gauge. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STL RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/12/2022
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 942382
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/12/2022
Comments: On January 12, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow up site inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. This inspection is to follow up on a spill of production fluid outside of containment that occurred on January 8, 2022. At the time of inspection, contractors where excavating the area in front of the infiltration berm off the southwest corner of the well pad. The depth of the excavation was about 4 to 5 ft. The area of the infiltration berm that had yet to be excavated had a conductivity greater than 4,000 uS/cm. The design of the trench along the west end of the pad caused production fluid to flow to the southwest corner also. The southwest area of the pad also has a drainage culvert with the outlet pipe draining to the infiltration berm. The pooled production fluid in the northwest infiltration berm has been vacuumed out. The conductivity of the soil in front of that infiltration berm was over 4,000 uS/cm. No excavation has been done to this area. The northwest plunge pool filled back with water. The conductivity of the water was over 4,000 uS/cm. A sample was collected from the plunge pool and will be analyzed for SAC code 942. Mr. Rodriguez thinks that the seal around the outlet pipe from the drainage culvert in that area is failing, resulting in water in the plunge pool. There were no new seeps or areas where the production fluid has appeared off the well pad edge. STL Resources plans to finish removing the impacted soil from the southwest infiltration berm and move to the northwest infiltration berm to begin removing impacted soil there. Mr. Rodriguez said that a vacuum truck was scheduled to vacuum out the water in the northwest plunge pool and the water that had drained into the culverts from the trench along the west end of the pad. The spill of production fluid off the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law 401. Clean Streams Law 402(b) is being supplanted by Clean Streams Law 401. Violations from Inspection Report 3305227 remain outstanding.

Comments: On 03/04/2025, a follow up inspection was conducted at the DMC Well site, for violations cited on 2/21/2025 (Inspection ID: 3922642, Enforcement ID: 438876).Violations included 78a57a, 78a54, 91.34(a) and SWMA 301.PA DEP conductivity probe calibrated on 03/04/2025.During the inspection the following was observed:-The Act 9 sign was present at site entrance (Photo 1).-The previously impacted area, noted in Inspection Report (IR) 3922642, located on the northwest side of the well pad was observed. A layer of a white, crusty substance was observed on the soil located in front of the large, gray electrical box noted in IR 3922642 (Photos 2-6).-Field conductivity screening was conducted near the large, gray electrical box. Field conductivity readings between 0.993 ms/cm (993 s/cm) and 14.17 ms/cm were observed. This area had not been previously remediated due to the proximity to the electrical equipment, as discussed with the operator (Photos 7-11).-Pooled fluid was observed located directly adjacent to secondary containment. An elevated field conductivity reading of 18.60 ms/cm was observed within the fluid. The discharge onto the ground and failure to dispose of fluids, specifically produced fluid, are violations of 78a.54, 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act (SWMA) 301. The potential to have indirectly impacted Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC) is a violation of 91.34(a). Outstanding violations are being issued for the pooled fluid demonstrating elevated conductivity (Photos 12-14).-Damp material was observed along the edge of the secondary containment. An elevated field conductivity reading of 8.74 ms/cm was observed (Photos 15-16).-Pooled fluid was observed on a driving lane near the site entrance on the northeast side of the well pad. Field conductivity readings between 0.470 ms/cm (470 s/cm) and 5.85 ms/cm were observed (Photos 17-21).Determination:Outstanding violations issued.

Comments: Routine field inspection performed in afternoon with cool, cloudy weather conditions, and 43 degrees. Last inspection performed on 6/5/16, more than 6 years ago. Wellhead is located in Agriculture field planted with corn that has been harvested ~750' NE of surface/ground production equipment (photo #1). properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: KENDRA DISP LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/08/2024
Violation Code: 102.5(m)4 - PERMIT REQUIREMENTS – GENERAL PERMITS – Person failed to comply with the terms and conditions of the E & S Control General Permit.
Violation ID: 8187018
Permit API: 033-27255
Unconventional: No
County: Clearfield
Municipality: Brady Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/08/2024
Comments: Routine site inspection on May 8, 2024 with site manager Rob Platt. The Zelman UIC site is fully operational at this time but the site was idle at time of inspection. The last time this UIC received brine fluids was February 2024. Kendra Disposal is currently in contract negotiations with waste operators. I did a walk around site during the inspection. Please note, several areas of concern were observed during the inspection. The slope to the mechanical building has a lot of rills on the hillside resulting in erosion and sedimentation issues (photo 1). Compost sock has been installed to help collect run-off before entering into the truckers off-loading building (photo 2). The hillside has not been seeded and mulched per the E and S plans. This has been noted in multiple inspection reports since earth work started for this project over a year ago. In addition, the slope to the tank farm remains exposed. Rills are occurring on this cut-slope and sediment is collecting in the rock lined ditch. The cut-slope never had E and S blanket reapplied per the E and S plans (photos 5-7). The rock line ditch was never properly installed and/or completed after the tank farm pad was constructed. The rock line ditch just stops and doesn't connect to the sediment trap like is should according to the E and S plans (photos 8-10). Erosion is occurring along the access roads as well. Sediment is building up on the rock filters. Violations have been cited. The Department recommends addressing these issues.In addition to a site inspection at the Zelman UIC, historical background stream monitoring samples were collected at three nearby streams. Stream samples will be tested for SAC 046 plus lead and copper. These samples were sent to the Departments Lab in Harrisburg for testing. Results will be provided to the operator electronically upon receiving them.
